message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (titled *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series; introduces the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Continues Harry’s adventures at Hogwarts; introduces the mystery of the Chamber. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Features Sirius Black and the introduction of the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Introduces the Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s denial of Voldemort’s return. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince** | 2005 | Provides backstory on Voldemort’s Horcruxes and deepens the plot. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Concludes the main saga with the final battle against Voldemort. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 (book) / 2016 (film) | A companion guide to the wizarding creatures featured in the Harry Potter films. |
| **Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald** (novelization) | 2018 | Novel adaptation of the second film in the Fantastic Beasts series. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a political thriller set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut crime novel under her pseudonym; follows private detective Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book featuring Cormoran Strike. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free online story during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |

These titles represent the core of Rowling’s bibliography and include both her celebrated fantasy series and her ventures into adult fiction and other genres.
